overview: Panama is the southernmost country in Central America, where it joins South America. Its capital and largest city is Panama City. Panama became independent from Colombia in 1903. The Panama Canal, opened in 1914, links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans and is one of the most important shipping routes in the world.

geography.text: Panama is a narrow, S-shaped strip of land with the Caribbean Sea to the north and the Pacific Ocean to the south. Mountains run along its spine, and much of the land is tropical forest. The Darién region, on the border with Colombia, is dense rainforest that no road crosses.

history.text: Panama's narrow strip of land has always been a crossing point; Spanish treasure from Peru was carried across it to the Atlantic. It became part of Colombia after independence from Spain, then broke away with US support in 1903. The United States built the Panama Canal and controlled it until handing it over to Panama in 1999.

events.title: Balboa sees the Pacific
events.text: Vasco Núñez de Balboa crosses Panama and becomes the first European to see the Pacific from the Americas.

events.title: Canal opens
events.text: The Panama Canal opens to shipping.

events.title: US invasion
events.text: US forces remove the military ruler Manuel Noriega.

events.title: Canal handed over
events.text: Panama takes full control of the canal.

government.text: Panama is a presidential republic. The President is elected for a five-year term and cannot serve two terms in a row. Panama took full control of the Panama Canal from the United States in 1999. It has no army; it abolished it after the US invasion of 1989.

economy.text: The Panama Canal is the heart of Panama's economy, earning billions in tolls each year. Banking, shipping, trade through the Colón Free Zone and the Panama ship register, one of the largest in the world, are also important. Panama uses the US dollar alongside its own coins.

culture.text: Panama sits where North and South America meet, and its culture mixes Indigenous, African, Spanish and Caribbean influences. The Guna people of the San Blas islands make molas, colourful layered textiles. Panama's old town, Casco Viejo, is a UNESCO site.

items.title: The Panama Canal
items.text: Opened in 1914; a new set of larger locks opened in 2016.

items.title: Molas
items.text: Hand-stitched panels made by Guna women.

sport.text: Baseball and football are the most popular sports. Mariano Rivera, from Panama, is Major League Baseball's all-time leader in saves. Panama played at its first men's World Cup in 2018.

items.title: Mariano Rivera
items.text: The first player voted unanimously into baseball's Hall of Fame.
Irving Saladino won Panama's first Olympic gold, in the long jump.

didYouKnow: In Panama you can watch the sun rise over the Pacific and set over the Atlantic.
Each year about 13,000 ships pass through the Panama Canal.
